evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/nfc/NFCAccessController.ts:118-119 — startAccessSession(credentialId) resolves an explicitly-passed credential via credentialManager.getCredentialById(credentialId), which (NFCCredentialManager.ts:150-152) only matches on id and does NOT check status or validUntil. The auto-select branch (line 121) uses getActiveCredentials() which filters `status === 'active' && validUntil > now` (NFCCredentialManager.ts:140-144). So the explicit-id path starts an access session (and proceeds to transmit) with an expired or revoked credential that the auto-select path would reject — a client-side credential-validation gap / defense-in-depth inconsistency. Fix: have startAccessSession re-validate the resolved credential's status/validUntil regardless of whether the id was supplied explicitly.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/widgets/WidgetDataProvider.ts:376-380 — the request() catch block swallows every failure (non-2xx and network) and returns `{} as T` as a 'mock data fallback'. The empty object is cast across the API boundary and handed to widget renderers, so a failed/unauthorized fetch is indistinguishable from an empty-but-successful response: widgets silently render blank/default data instead of surfacing an error or stale-data state, and the only signal is a __DEV__-gated console.error. Consider returning a typed error/empty-state marker the widget layer can detect rather than an untyped `{} as T`.
